articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Permanent Magnet Machines' (Digest No.92)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines
IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines
abstract: The principles of operation of brushless drive systems are reviewed by the authors and examples are given of various motor topologies which have been developed. General design considerations, as well as developments in analysis and CAD procedures, are also discussed. In addition applications of brushless motors in various market sectors are considered, and some of the possibilities for the newly emerging grades of permanent magnet materials are highlighted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Permanent magnet generators for aerospace applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines
abstract: The primary design consideration for electrical generators used in aerospace applications is the maximisation of the power to weight ratio (power density). Since the gross power available from a generator is directly proportional to its operating speed and the generated frequency is unconstrained in an isolated system, it is natural to operate at high speeds. This high speed operation makes the use of a DC rotor field impractical due to brush wear, and therefore the field excitation is obtained from permanent magnets (PM). Many magnetic circuit configurations have been proposed by various researchers on PM machines, but there have been few attempts at quantitative comparisons. The author aims to provide such comparisons for popular configurations, in the power range 0.25-10 kW and the speed range 10000-100000 RPM suitable for unmanned aircraft and spacecraft. The general approach is to produce approximate designs for each configuration over the power and speed ranges, using formal optimisation methods, and then to compare the power density figures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a high-speed permanent magnet motor
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines
abstract: The authors describe the design of a high-speed hand-held precision instrument suitable for surgical work in dentistry and medicine. This instrument is capable of delivering 10 W to the cutting tool at a speed of 150000 r.p.m. The final design is somewhat unusual and consists of a miniature synchronous motor having a rare-earth cobalt rotor magnet of only 3 mm diameter and 7 mm axial length. The 3-phase motor is supplied at 2.5 kHz by three in-line transformers having single-turn secondary windings which are connected to the motor stator winding. This consists simply of three bars and an end-ring and is machined as a single component.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PM DC motors with series field characteristics
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines
abstract: Small DC motors are expanding in use on vehicles, in the home, in industry and in the office and the availability of low cost ferrite magnets makes the permanent magnet (PM) motor most attractive. The author shows how many nonreversible applications could benefit from a 'series' characteristic and in most cases can provide a lower cost than the normal PM DC motor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines
abstract: Permanent magnets are used in a wide range of industrial, domestic, automotive and aerospace applications. The current uses of permanent magnets in domestic applications averages 50 per household in Western Europe. The total permanent magnet sales in 1985 are valued at Pounds 780*10/sup 6/ and this market is expected to expand at 10% per annum for the coming years. The author describes the processing, properties and uses of the two major groups of permanent magnetic materials produced by powder processing. These are the hard ferrite and rare earth permanent magnet groups.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines
abstract: There are many configurations of permanent magnet machine, some of them are more significant than others. Machines are most commonly 3-phase but single phase capacitor start and run designs can be very effective. There is an ever widening choice of magnet materials available, but the most useful are the ferrites and the rare earths, whether samarium cobalt or neodymium-iron-boron. The choice of magnet depends on the specification, with initial cost and operating temperature having an important role. The author examines motor characteristics for three types of permanent magnet synchronous motors and assesses the cost effectiveness of each type.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines
abstract: Stepping motors are characterised by their ability to translate switched excitation changes into precisely defined increments in rotor position. This makes them an inherently digital device ideally suited to numerically controlled servo systems, with applications ranging from multi-kilowatt drives for steering radio antenna to numerous low power applications in the computer peripheral markets. The author reviews the principles of operation of both hybrid and permanent magnet stepping motors. The relative merits of different motor topologies are outlined and methods of analysis and design discussed. Finally design examples based on rare earth and Alnico magnets are compared.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
